newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: VMC to temporarily shut milling operations.
newsitem.headline: VMC to temporarily shut milling operations.

text.p: Financially-troubled Victorias Milling Co said on Tuesday it had temporarily shut down its raw sugar mill and sugar refinery starting today.
"This is the first time in the 78 years of Victoria's history that we are going to shut down our sugar mill operations," Victorias' public affairs manager Ernest Latiza told Reuters.
He said the shutdown was due to lack of sugar cane and raw sugar as well as for off-season repair.
Victorias is one of the biggest sugar companies in the country with capacity to mill 15,000 tonnes of raw sugar every day and refine 25,000 bags of sugar each day.
Latiza said the sugar operation will resume on October 1.
"We will start getting sugar cane by the last week of September," he added.
Latiza said Victorias would keep a skeletal workforce out of the total 4,500 workers during the shutdown and might retrench some of them when operations resumed.
The workers will still receive their bonuses and dues to be given to them on a staggered basis.
Latiza said it was not yet known how much would be lost due to the shutdown and workers' pay package.
Victorias is currently deep in debt as a result of a sharp downturn in sugar prices and growing competition in the industry.
It was recently granted a reprieve from debt payment by the Securities and Exchange Commission to allow it to restructure its organisation.
Victorias owes 5.07 billion pesos ($192 million) of debt to 32 bank creditors.
